title: Playing 'Sassie Paris' during the executions
summary: At a stadium outside Ankara they waited for a whistle, played on cue and learned later that twelve politicians had just been condemned and hanged; their chauffeur was seized when they tried to see the bodies.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: So we went. The next morning, cars were waiting for us and they took us to Ankara, and we went to hotels and from the hotels we were taken out about ten kilometers from the City of Ankara, to what you would call kind of a stadium, with a great big awning on it.
Right.
Briggs

And everything else was set. So, one of the officers, he said, "You can have -- take a dressing room, you can relax in your dressing room, but at 8:00 be ready, dressed and everything else." So, we relaxed, and at 8:00, we were ready to -- tuned our horns and everything else. We still didn't know what's happening. So, at 8:00 o'clock, they had given us refreshments, and at 9:00 o'clock, nothing happened. I'd say about 9:30, an officer came and he said, "Take your seats, get ready to play." He said, "I want you to --." He said, "When you hear a whistle, you play 'Sassie Paris'."
"Sassie Paris".
Yeh. So he said, "We're looking at you." We don't know what to think of -- I'm so nervous 'cause I'm living through what happened. We didn't know what to do, looking
Briggs 162

at each other, couldn't say nothing, 'cause if you spoke French, you don't understand it, and you spoke English and he doesn't understand it. So, it was just one of those things. Well, at a quarter to ten, another officer came in and said, "Are you all set, you're ready?" We said, "Yes, we're ready." He said, "Take your positions as though you're going to play, ready to play. This is Mezz and me putting our horns in our mouths.
So, sitting here with your horn?
Yes. (Laughter).
In your hotel room?

Yes, fifteen minutes. Saxophones, pianist, we were waiting for this whistle to blow. At last the whistle blew, and we did "Sassie Paris", but fortunately we knew the number by heart. The lights went out, they extinguished the lights. It was represented -- we find out after that the twelve most prominent politicians
Briggs

in Turkey, and one name I do remember because I'd read often about him, Dagid Bey, the twelve of them were executed and hanged. They were condemned at 10:00 o'clock in the evening. They were condemned at 9:00 o'clock in the evening, and hanged at 10:00 in the marketplace of Ankara. I'll tell you the rest in a minute. We found that out through our chauffeur, the chauffeur that came to take us back to the hotel. We tried to -- we bribed the chauffeur to take us to the marketplace, because he said that the bodies were still hanging. But before we could get to the marketplace, soldiers stopped us, and the poor guy disappeared, we don't know what happened to him.
You mean they pulled him out of the car.
They pulled him out of the car, and had taken us to our hotels.
Briggs
We don't know what happened to that poor man. He was hollering and screaming and everything else. I don't know what happened.

They took us to our hotels, and gave instructions for us to be enclosed in our rooms. We were not supposed to leave our rooms until they come to get us the following morning to take us back to Para-Constantinople.
And that's what happened.
